1	\section{Analysis}
2	\label{sec:analysis}
3	
4	The regime-dependent pattern in \S\ref{sec:main-results} establishes \emph{where} SICA succeeds and fails. This section investigates \emph{why}: trace correlation quantifies the SC plateau (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}), supporting diagnostics confirm the mechanism (Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}), and remediation analysis reveals a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
5	
6	\subsection{Condorcet Effective-K}
7	\label{sec:effective-k}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:independence} reports Fleiss' $\kappa$ and Effective-K (Eq.~\ref{eq:effk}) across 15 conditions at $K = 12$. Among instruction-tuned models, $\kappa$ ranges from 0.21 to 0.82, yielding $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20\text{--}3.62$. Qwen3-14B in thinking mode reaches $\kappa = 0.91$ ($K_{\text{eff}} = 1.09$). The four Mistral-7B FOLIO seeds produce $\kappa \in [0.41, 0.51]$ ($K_{\text{eff}} \approx 1.8\text{--}2.2$), yet $\Delta$ ranges from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp---seed-level constraint quality, not independence, drives the variation. Two conditions are jointly necessary for positive $\Delta$: sufficient $K_{\text{eff}}$ (Qwen conditions with $K_{\text{eff}} \leq 1.30$ never improve) and sufficient SC accuracy (Mistral on ProofWriter with the highest $K_{\text{eff}} = 3.62$ but SC $= 39\%$ produces significant degradation). Even when both hold, sampling variance determines whether the constraint pool is discriminative. Cross-model validation with three families confirms universality: Mistral-7B ($\kappa = 0.44$), LLaMA-3.1-8B ($\kappa = 0.41$), Qwen2.5-7B ($\kappa = 0.66$), and Qwen2.5-14B ($\kappa = 0.74$) all produce $\kappa$ well above zero (Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-model-kappa}).

40	\subsection{Supporting Diagnostic Analyses}
41	
42	Four additional analyses confirm the mechanism underlying SICA's failure. Extraction error taxonomy (Appendix~\ref{app:extraction}): 91.8\% of constraints are technically discriminative, but their discriminative direction mirrors the majority answer; 42.9\% of constraints are redundant across traces (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality}), quantifying how co-sourcing from the same model produces near-duplicate formalizations. Removing the 8.2\% non-discriminative constraints yields zero improvement. Constraint ablation (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}): on Mistral-7B ($n = 804$, FOLIO + ProofWriter pooled), MAX-SAT and count-only agree on 94.4\% of predictions, with disagreements split nearly evenly (18 vs.\ 17); the solver's weighted satisfiability computation adds no value over simple constraint counting because constraint weights carry information redundant with vote counts (Eq.~\ref{eq:degenerate}). Per-domain, MAX-SAT provides a marginal edge in the intermediate-SC region (59.3\% vs.\ count-only 56.9\%) but actively hurts in the Type~C regime (36.5\% vs.\ 37.2\%), mirroring the regime-dependent pattern of SICA itself. Hyperparameter sensitivity (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}): $K = 12$ is the only setting with $\Delta > 2$\,pp among five $K$ values, and only $T = 0.7$ among four temperatures yields a positive effect; both peaks coincide with relatively low SC baselines rather than reflecting hyperparameter effects per se. Entropy decomposition (Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}): all SICA effects concentrate in high-entropy problems ($\Delta$ up to $+12.8$\,pp in the intermediate-SC region), but the direction depends on the accuracy regime---high entropy signals correctable uncertainty only when the model has partial knowledge.
43	
44	\subsection{Remediation Analysis}
45	\label{sec:remediation}
46	\label{sec:interventions}
47	
48	We test twelve remediation strategies: nine prompt-level spanning six dimensions (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:remediation}) and three method-level (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). All nine prompt-level strategies fail. Contrastive prompting reduces non-discriminative constraints from 8.2\% to 6.0\% but newly discriminative constraints still mirror the majority ($\Delta = -1.1$\,pp). Cross-model extraction fails in both directions: weaker models extracting from stronger traces yield 0\% discriminative constraints; stronger models extracting from weaker traces produce accuracy within $\pm$1\,pp of self-extraction. Only 1 of 4 temperature settings yields a positive effect ($p = 0.092$); multi-temperature sampling produces $\Delta = 0.00$\,pp.
49	
50	\paragraph{Method-level interventions.} Three method-level strategies target different aspects of the independence bottleneck on Mistral-7B (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}). Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from premises. Despite producing objectively superior constraints---higher Z3 compilation, lower redundancy (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality})---ICG yields $\Delta \approx 0$ across three seeds (McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). Per-constraint-set reranking produces $\kappa = 0.47$, nearly identical to SC's $\kappa = 0.44$: the bottleneck is a property of the model itself, not an artifact of trace co-sourcing. Contrastive scoring generates pro and con constraints per candidate but yields $\Delta = -9.31$\,pp on FOLIO ($p < 0.01$) and $-4.50$\,pp on LogiQA (n.s.); 62.7\% of constraints are trivially satisfied, explaining systematic degeneration (Appendices~\ref{app:constraint-quality},~\ref{app:error-categorization}). Debate adds a proposer-critic-defense chain, producing $\Delta = -18.63$\,pp and $-23.00$\,pp ($p < 0.001$ on both datasets), with discordant pairs heavily skewed toward correct$\to$wrong flips (Appendix~\ref{app:error-categorization}). Three of six method-dataset conditions reach significance, all negative.

71	\paragraph{Independence-accuracy trade-off.} Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization} compares Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods on Mistral-7B FOLIO and adds SC from three model families for cross-architecture validation. On Mistral-7B, SC ($\kappa = 0.44$), Diverse-Prompt ($\kappa = 0.40$), and ICG ($\kappa = 0.47$) cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, forming a same-model ceiling. Debate breaks through to $\kappa = 0.15$ (Eff-$K = 4.44$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp. All three model families cluster above $\kappa = 0.40$, confirming the ceiling is architecture-independent (Appendix~\ref{app:cross-model-kappa}). This constitutes a Pareto frontier (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}): methods that increase trace independence destroy accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. The only demonstrated path past this frontier requires signal from outside the model's distribution, consistent with the oracle result (\S\ref{sec:oracle}) and published systems that bypass self-extraction \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm}.

4	\subsection{Setup}
5	\label{sec:exp-setup}
6	
7	We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models on three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances.
8	
9	\paragraph{Models.} Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen3-14B (non-thinking mode)~\citep{yang2024qwen25}, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3~\citep{jiang2023mistral}, LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct~\citep{dubey2024llama3}, and QwQ-32B~\citep{qwen2024qwq} (7B--32B parameters).

GSM8K~\citep{cobbe2021gsm8k} ($n{=}30$) and AIME 2024 ($n{=}22$) probe the degenerate regime ($C_0 < 5\%$).
12	
13	\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$; extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$. Z3 timeout: 10s. $\alpha{=}0.5$. Statistical significance via McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs from 10,000 resamples for $n \geq 200$.

No seed reaches $p < 0.05$; the 4-seed mean is $+1.47$\,pp. Mistral-7B on LogiQA, despite the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), attributable to domain formalizability (Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}).
63	
64	\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): confirmation bias.} Nine conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 2{,}800$) produce no significant positive effects. Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break confirmation bias.
65	
66	\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning.
67	
68	\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.
69	
70	Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence: the intermediate-SC region is narrow and observed only for Mistral-7B on FOLIO.

80	\subsection{Oracle Control}
81	\label{sec:oracle}
82	
83	Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and DSL from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$) and 86.67\% on ProofWriter ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter) of problems.
84	
85	These results establish that the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound given discriminative constraints. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 24.1\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling. The remaining 75.9\% is lost to self-extraction quality.
86	
87	
88	\subsection{Four-Seed Replication}
89	\label{sec:replication}
90	
91	We replicate the intermediate-SC result with four seeds on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$, $K = 12$, $T = 0.7$). Effects range from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp (mean $+1.47$\,pp); 2 of 4 seeds show marginal trends ($p < 0.10$), none reaches $p < 0.05$. Seeds~42 and~456 share identical SC baselines (55.88\%) yet produce different outcomes ($+3.43$ vs.\ $0.00$\,pp), indicating that seed-level constraint quality---not SC level alone---drives the effect. The entropy decomposition in Appendix~\ref{app:entropy} confirms that the aggregate $\Delta$ is driven by high-entropy problems: seed~42 achieves $+12.8$\,pp on this partition while seed~456 shows $-1.3$\,pp.

We evaluate SICA against Self-Consistency (SC) across six models on three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances.

\paragraph{Intermediate-SC region.} Mistral-7B on FOLIO (SC $\sim$50--55\%) shows positive directional trends in 2 of 4 seeds: $\Delta = +3.43$\,pp ($p = 0.092$) and $+2.94$\,pp ($p = 0.070$); the remaining seeds show null or negative results. No seed reaches $p < 0.05$; the 4-seed mean is $+1.47$\,pp. Mistral-7B on LogiQA, despite the same SC range, yields only $\Delta = +0.50$\,pp ($p = 1.0$), attributable to domain formalizability (Appendix~\ref{app:failure-modes}).

\paragraph{Type A (SC $\geq$ 60\%): confirmation bias.} Nine conditions with SC $\geq 63\%$ (combined $N > 2{,}800$) produce no significant positive effects. Qwen2.5-14B on ProofWriter shows significant degradation ($\Delta = -2.50$\,pp, $p = 0.011$). Even in-context learning with gold FOL examples ($\Delta = +0.50$\,pp, n.s.) cannot break confirmation bias.

\paragraph{Type C (SC $\leq$ 40\%): error amplification.} Mistral-7B on ProofWriter ($n = 600$, SC $= 39.33\%$) shows $\Delta = -2.83$\,pp ($p = 0.014$): SICA \emph{significantly hurts} by formalizing incorrect reasoning.

\paragraph{Degenerate cases.} When $C_0 < 5\%$, nearly all traces agree and SICA reduces to SC by construction.

Figure~\ref{fig:regime-scatter} visualizes the regime dependence: the intermediate-SC region is narrow and observed only for Mistral-7B on FOLIO.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{f2_regime_scatter}
\caption{SICA $\Delta$ (pp) vs.\ SC baseline. Filled: $n \geq 100$; open: $n < 100$. The intermediate-SC region (50--55\%, shaded) contains the only positive trends (none reaching $p < 0.05$). Type~C: significant degradation ($p = 0.014$).}
\label{fig:regime-scatter}
\end{figure}


\subsection{Oracle Control}
\label{sec:oracle}

Oracle variants replace self-extracted constraints with gold annotations: FOL from FOLIO ($n = 204$) and DSL from ProofWriter ($n = 600$). Oracle-SICA achieves 89.71\% on FOLIO ($\Delta = +14.22$\,pp, $p = 2.0 \times 10^{-7}$) and 86.67\% on ProofWriter ($\Delta = +11.50$\,pp, $p = 9.21 \times 10^{-15}$). Z3 agrees with gold labels on 95.1\% (FOLIO) and 97.1\% (ProofWriter) of problems.

These results establish that the MAX-SAT mechanism is sound given discriminative constraints. Mistral-7B's best self-extracted result ($+3.43$\,pp) captures only 24.1\% of the FOLIO oracle ceiling. The remaining 75.9\% is lost to self-extraction quality.


\subsection{Four-Seed Replication}
\label{sec:replication}

We replicate the intermediate-SC result with four seeds on Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$, $K = 12$, $T = 0.7$). Effects range from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp (mean $+1.47$\,pp); 2 of 4 seeds show marginal trends ($p < 0.10$), none reaches $p < 0.05$. Seeds~42 and~456 share identical SC baselines (55.88\%) yet produce different outcomes ($+3.43$ vs.\ $0.00$\,pp), indicating that seed-level constraint quality---not SC level alone---drives the effect. The entropy decomposition in Appendix~\ref{app:entropy} confirms that the aggregate $\Delta$ is driven by high-entropy problems: seed~42 achieves $+12.8$\,pp on this partition while seed~456 shows $-1.3$\,pp.

3. **C3 (NEW): Process-κ + Independence Quantification** — cosine 0.69 >> answer-κ 0.41; κ=0.21–0.82; universal across 3 families
4. **C4: Regime-Dependent Pattern + Diagnostics** — 3 failure modes; C0+SC diagnostic; entropy decomposition

### §2 Related Work (0.70pp)
- SC and extensions (5-6 refs): Wang 2023, USC, Loo 2025, Taubenfeld 2025, DiVeRSe
- Neuro-symbolic (6 refs): Logic-LM, LINC, DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer, LogicAgent → all use external; we test self-extraction
- CJT/voting (4 refs): Condorcet, Ladha 1992, Lefort 2024 → we extend to symbolic extraction
- Verification (3 refs): ORM, PRM, Math-Shepherd → trained verifier paradigm
- Self-correction parallels (2 refs): Huang 2024, Stechly 2025 → parallel to our confirmation bias
- Debate (2 refs): Liang 2023, Du 2023 → different regime
- [MINOR PATCH: add confirmation bias parallel to self-correction literature]

### §3 Method (1.20pp)

**§3.1 SC and Condorcet (300w)** — KEEP
- SC as majority voting; CJT guarantee; Eff-K formula (Eq. 1)

**§3.2 SICA Pipeline (400w)** — KEEP
- Trace gen → extraction → dedup → MAX-SAT → scoring
- Degeneration under confirmation bias (Eq. 4)
- C0 diagnostic (Eq. 5)
- Figure 1: Pipeline diagram

**§3.3 Oracle Control (200w)** — KEEP
- Gold FOL replaces self-extracted; causal isolation

**§3.4 Process-Level Independence (150w)** — NEW
- Define process-κ: pairwise CoT cosine similarity (TF-IDF)
- Motivation: answer-κ may underestimate true bottleneck
- If traces reason similarly but reach different answers → answer-κ overestimates independence
- Applicable to all LLM trace aggregation

**§3.5 Scope (100w)** — PATCH
- Same-model self-extraction
- 25+ remediation strategies tested (9 prompt + 3 method + 13 additional)

### §4 Experiments (1.50pp)

**§4.1 Setup (250w)** — MINOR PATCH
- 6 models, 3 domains + diagnostics, K=12, T=0.7
- [ADD] mention confirmation bias and process-κ experiments

**§4.2 Main Results (500w)** — KEEP

**§4.3 Oracle Control (200w)** — KEEP

### §5 Analysis (1.70pp) — MAJOR RESTRUCTURE

**§5.1 Condorcet Effective-K (300w)** — KEEP
- Table 3: κ and Eff-K across 15 conditions
- Cross-model: 3 families κ≥0.41; architecture-independent ceiling
- Dual requirement: sufficient Eff-K AND sufficient SC

**§5.2 Symbolic Confirmation Bias (250w)** — NEW
- Key metrics from exp-confirmation-bias:
  - SICA-correct: gold constraint rate 78.1%, bias ratio 0.28
  - SICA-incorrect: wrong constraint rate 83.3%, bias ratio 4.97×
  - 94% SICA errors overlap SC errors
  - 12 correct flips from minority trace diversity (43% gold support)
- Causal chain: model→answer→FOL confirms answer→aggregation≈SC
- CEGIS validation: refinement doesn't help (oscillates)
- Quality Ladder: cross-model extraction ≈ self-extraction << oracle

**§5.3 Process-Level Independence (200w)** — NEW
- Mistral-7B FOLIO-204 results:
  - CoT cosine similarity: 0.69
  - Answer-κ: 0.41
  - Correlation: r=-0.06, p=0.36 (uncorrelated)
  - Convergent reasoning pairs: 9.3%
- Answer-κ is lower bound on true independence bottleneck
- Even methods targeting answer diversity may not break process-level correlation

**§5.4 Supporting Diagnostics (200w)** — COMPRESS
- Extraction taxonomy: 91.8% discriminative, direction mirrors majority → Appendix
- 42.9% redundant constraints → Appendix
- MAX-SAT ablation: 94.4% agreement with count-only → Appendix
- K/T sensitivity: isolated peaks, SC-confounded → Appendix
- Entropy: all effects in high-entropy, direction regime-dependent → Appendix

- **Prompt-level (9 strategies, 6 dimensions)**: all fail (compressed, Table in Appendix)
- **Method-level (Table 4)**: ICG neutral, Contrastive harmful, Debate catastrophic
- **13 Additional Directions**: all negative (compressed 1-2 sentences each, full table in Appendix)

- **Cross-model κ**: 3 families all κ≥0.41 → architecture-independent ceiling
- **Pareto frontier**: only external signal breaks through (consistent with oracle)

### §6 Discussion (0.40pp) — MODERATE REWRITE
- Oracle causally isolates extraction as binding bottleneck
- [NEW] Symbolic Confirmation Bias as unifying root cause:
  - Direct channel (voting diversity) + indirect channel (constraint homogenization) unified
  - 25+ failures explained by single mechanism: self-extraction inherits model bias
- [NEW] Process-κ implication: bottleneck deeper than answer-level metrics suggest
- Statistical evidence: 0 significant positives vs multiple significant negatives
- Published methods (DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer) bypass self-extraction → consistent with diagnosis
- Scale: κ increases with scale (Qwen 7B→14B); 70B+ open
- Three paths: trained extractors, external provers, multi-model pipelines

- SICA across 6 models, 3 families, 3 domains, N>3,000
- [NEW] Root cause: Symbolic Confirmation Bias (4.97×)
- [NEW] Process-κ: cosine 0.69 >> answer-κ 0.41

1	---
2	name: paper-writing-norms
3	description: 顶会级别论文写作风格规范——章节写法（Abstract/Intro/Related Work）、去 AI 风格、视觉密度、叙事哲学。Paper Agent 和 Worker 写论文章节时必须加载。
4	allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep]
5	scope: global
6	version: 2
7	priority: 9
8	tags:
9	  - writing
10	  - paper
11	  - style
12	  - norms
13	roles:
14	  - agent
15	  - worker
16	  - paper_agent
17	---
18	
19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证

- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**

- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim

1	\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
2	
3	Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
4	The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
5	SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
6	\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
7	The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.
8	
9	Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
10	Trained reward models \citep{lightman2024prm, wang2024mathshepherd} and diversity-aware sampling \citep{diverseaware2026} break the plateau by injecting external signal, but require trained verifiers or sampling modifications.
11	A more fundamental question remains: can \emph{structured aggregation} over symbolic representations extract information from the same traces that majority voting cannot?
12	
13	Recent neuro-symbolic methods suggest that formal reasoning can complement LLM generation.
14	Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, and LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent} each report gains on logical reasoning benchmarks, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
15	A simpler question precedes these extensions: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
16	Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
17	Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.
18	This motivates our study of Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
19	
20	We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth as $K$ grows \citep{austensmith1996}.
21	When independence fails, as \citet{ladha1992correlated} show for correlated voters, additional samples carry diminishing information.
22	We measure inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa} and find values from 0.21 to 0.82 across instruction-tuned conditions (0.91 for thinking mode), yielding Eff-$K = 1.20\text{--}3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$ (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
23	At Eff-$K \approx 2$, traces beyond $K = 12$ add negligible independent information---a scaling ceiling that applies to SC itself, not only to symbolic aggregation.
24	When the same model both produces traces and extracts constraints, the constraints inherit the traces' biases \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, kambhampati2024position}.
25	We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}: self-extracted constraints cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires for aggregation to surpass SC.
26	\citet{lefort2024condorcet_llm} examine CJT violations in LLM ensembles, but no prior study connects this framework to symbolic constraint extraction.
27	
28	We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
29	The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods shows that Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling Eff-$K$, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
30	This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches.
31	Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
32	Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail.
33	A directional positive trend occurs in one model-dataset condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO, 2 of 4 seeds with $p < 0.10$, none reaching $p < 0.05$; best $+3.43$\,pp), but only in a narrow band around 50--55\% SC; outside it, constraints echo the majority (Type~A) or amplify errors (Type~C).
34	The bottleneck is structural at the 7B--14B scale tested; whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome it remains open.
35	
36	Our contributions are:
37	\begin{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.

Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
Trained reward models \citep{lightman2024prm, wang2024mathshepherd} and diversity-aware sampling \citep{diverseaware2026} break the plateau by injecting external signal, but require trained verifiers or sampling modifications.
A more fundamental question remains: can \emph{structured aggregation} over symbolic representations extract information from the same traces that majority voting cannot?

Recent neuro-symbolic methods suggest that formal reasoning can complement LLM generation.
Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, and LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent} each report gains on logical reasoning benchmarks, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
A simpler question precedes these extensions: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.
This motivates our study of Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).

We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth as $K$ grows \citep{austensmith1996}.
When independence fails, as \citet{ladha1992correlated} show for correlated voters, additional samples carry diminishing information.
We measure inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa} and find values from 0.21 to 0.82 across instruction-tuned conditions (0.91 for thinking mode), yielding Eff-$K = 1.20\text{--}3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$ (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
At Eff-$K \approx 2$, traces beyond $K = 12$ add negligible independent information---a scaling ceiling that applies to SC itself, not only to symbolic aggregation.
When the same model both produces traces and extracts constraints, the constraints inherit the traces' biases \citep{huang2024selfcorrect, kambhampati2024position}.
We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}: self-extracted constraints cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires for aggregation to surpass SC.
\citet{lefort2024condorcet_llm} examine CJT violations in LLM ensembles, but no prior study connects this framework to symbolic constraint extraction.

We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods shows that Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling Eff-$K$, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches.
Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling.
Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail.
A directional positive trend occurs in one model-dataset condition (Mistral-7B on FOLIO, 2 of 4 seeds with $p < 0.10$, none reaching $p < 0.05$; best $+3.43$\,pp), but only in a narrow band around 50--55\% SC; outside it, constraints echo the majority (Type~A) or amplify errors (Type~C).
The bottleneck is structural at the 7B--14B scale tested; whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome it remains open.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Independence-Accuracy Trade-off (primary).} Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across four aggregation methods reveals a fundamental Pareto frontier: SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$ (a same-model ceiling), while Debate reduces $\kappa$ to 0.15 (Eff-$K = 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA). Twelve remediation strategies (nine prompt-level, three method-level) all fail, confirming that same-model aggregation cannot simultaneously achieve independence and accuracy (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).

\item \textbf{Independence Bottleneck and Diagnostic Tools.} Same-model traces yield Fleiss' $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ for $K = 12$), quantifying SC's own scaling ceiling: Eff-$K \approx 2$ means traces beyond $K = 12$ add negligible independent information for any aggregation method. The multi-candidate rate $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help (\S\ref{sec:condorcet}, \S\ref{sec:effective-k}).

\item \textbf{Oracle-Extraction Gap.} Oracle constraints yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$). Self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling, localizing the failure to extraction quality, not the symbolic approach (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).

\item \textbf{Regime-Dependent Pattern (directional).} A directional positive trend occurs in a narrow band ($\sim$50--55\% SC) in one model on one dataset (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp, none reaching $p < 0.05$). Three failure modes---confirmation bias, non-formalizability, error amplification---explain the regime boundaries (\S\ref{sec:main-results}).
\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Test-time computation scaling through multiple reasoning samples has emerged as a practical alternative to scaling model parameters \citep{snell2025scaling, guo2025deepseekr1}.
The dominant aggregation strategy, Self-Consistency (SC) \citep{wang2023sc}, samples $K$ chain-of-thought traces and selects the majority answer.
SC is simple, model-agnostic, and effective---but it is hitting a ceiling.
\citet{loo2025reevaluating} demonstrate that gains from increasing $K$ plateau and even decline for strong models.
The gap between SC's theoretical promise (independent correct voters converge to truth) and its practical behavior (saturating gains) points to a structural mismatch: same-model traces carry correlated errors, and majority voting has no mechanism to correct shared bias.

Confidence-weighted \citep{taubenfeld2025cisc} and universal \citep{chen2024usc} extensions alleviate this to a degree, but the core limitation persists.
Recent neuro-symbolic methods---Logic-LM \citep{pan2023logiclm}, LINC \citep{olausson2023linc}, DyLoS \citep{xu2026dylos}, Aristotle \citep{li2025aristotle}, FoVer \citep{wang2025fover}, LogicAgent \citep{luo2025logicagent}---each report gains on logical reasoning, but introduce components beyond the reasoning model: trained verifiers, solver selection, or external knowledge.
A simpler question precedes these: can the \emph{same} model that generates reasoning traces also extract useful formal constraints from them?
Self-extraction would be a zero-cost upgrade requiring no additional model, training data, or external prover.
Yet no prior work has systematically evaluated whether self-extracted constraints are useful for aggregation.

We ground our analysis in the Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) \citep{condorcet1785}: if $K$ independent voters each answer correctly with probability $p > 0.5$, the majority converges to truth \citep{austensmith1996}.
When independence fails \citep{ladha1992correlated}, additional samples carry diminishing information.
Measuring inter-trace agreement with Fleiss' $\kappa$ \citep{fleiss1971kappa}, we find $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ across instruction-tuned conditions, yielding Effective-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ for nominal $K = 12$: traces beyond a dozen add negligible independent information (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}).
The bottleneck runs deeper than answer-level agreement suggests.
Chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), revealing that traces share reasoning processes even when they diverge on final answers (\S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).
When the same model extracts FOL constraints from these correlated traces, the constraints exhibit \emph{symbolic confirmation bias}: on problems where the model errs, 83.3\% of self-extracted constraints support the wrong majority answer (bias ratio $4.97\times$), and 94\% of errors overlap with SC (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).
Self-extraction cannot supply the independent signal that CJT requires.

We study this through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA): extract FOL constraints from each of $K$ reasoning traces, deduplicate by syntactic equivalence, and select the answer best supported by a weighted partial MAX-SAT solution via Z3 \citep{demoura2008z3} (\S\ref{sec:pipeline}; Figure~\ref{fig:pipeline}).
We evaluate SICA across six models (7B--32B), three reasoning domains (FOLIO \citep{han2022folio}, ProofWriter \citep{tafjord2021proofwriter}, LogiQA \citep{liu2020logiqa}), and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication (Table~\ref{tab:main_results}).
More than twenty remediation strategies---spanning prompt engineering, method-level redesign, and ten additional directions targeting the independence bottleneck---all produce neutral or negative results, confirming the bottleneck is structural at the 7B--32B scale tested.

Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound: gold FOL yields $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling (\S\ref{sec:oracle}).
The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (tripling Eff-$K$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp; SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG all cluster at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$, forming a same-model ceiling that holds across three model families (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
Whether larger models or trained extractors can overcome this remains open.

Our contributions are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Independence-Accuracy Trade-off.} Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across four aggregation methods and three model families reveals a Pareto frontier: methods that increase independence destroy accuracy, while methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). More than twenty remediation strategies all fail (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).

\item \textbf{Symbolic Confirmation Bias.} Self-extracted constraints systematically confirm the model's majority answer: bias ratio $4.97\times$ on incorrect problems, 94\% error overlap with SC. The causal chain---model generates answer, extracts consistent FOL, Z3 aggregation mirrors majority vote---explains why self-extraction cannot correct errors the model has already committed (\S\ref{sec:confirmation-bias}).

\item \textbf{Process-Level Independence Quantification.} Chain-of-thought cosine similarity ($0.69$) far exceeds answer-level $\kappa$ ($0.41$), establishing that reasoning processes are more homogeneous than answer distributions suggest. Combined with Fleiss' $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ across 15 conditions and three model families, this quantifies the independence ceiling for same-model trace aggregation (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}, \S\ref{sec:process-kappa}).

\item \textbf{Regime-Dependent Pattern and Diagnostics.} Three failure modes---confirmation bias (SC $\geq 60\%$), non-formalizability, error amplification (SC $\leq 40\%$)---create regime boundaries. $C_0$ (multi-candidate rate) combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help (\S\ref{sec:main-results}).
\end{enumerate}

Symbolic constraints in first-order logic (FOL) appear to offer a way forward, but when extracted by the same model, they inherit the traces' correlation structure. We study it through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts FOL constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT. Methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches. The $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling, and $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic. The bottleneck is structural and universal---three model families (Mistral, LLaMA, Qwen) all exhibit $\kappa \geq 0.41$, and no aggregation method breaks through.
